features.title: The context pack is what napkin already says, numbered, under a budget
features.acceptance: The context pack for samples/window-in-existing-wall with the window selected and the shipped Connecticut pack loaded equals a hand-written golden item by item in the design note's order, its header item is the engine's No data explanation character for character after its label, and a pack over its word budget cuts the open lists first and the help second and never a design line.

features.title: The assistant's help is the help the repository ships
features.acceptance: The help embedded in the assistant module equals docs/building.md, rules-engine.md, shortcuts.md, viewer.md and first-run.md on disk, each splits at its level-two headings, the result-kind map returns its named sections, and the question "what is ground snow load" picks rules-engine.md's "In the app" among its three sections.

features.title: The answer guard refuses a sentence with a number napkin did not give
features.acceptance: The answer guard keeps a sentence whose every number token (integer, decimal, fraction, feet-inch length, lumber name, table or section designation, percentage or number word) occurs normalised in the context pack, and refuses any other sentence, and any reference to an item the pack does not have, in napkin's words naming what was said.

features.title: Sketch from words proposes rough planks only
features.acceptance: The design note's quick-bench sketch proposal becomes four rough-plank AddEntity requests with the exact snapped sizes and anchors, each malformed or over-limit part is refused line by line with its reason, an unknown member fails to parse, and a plan made against a sketch that has since changed is refused.

features.title: Edit in words proposes only the requests the panel already makes
features.acceptance: Each of the six edits in words maps to the request the panel makes on samples/coffee-table, a size off the 1/1024-inch grid, a stock not in the materials library or a part name matching two parts refuses its line, and an edit outside the closed set fails to parse.

features.title: The local runtime talks only to a model on this machine, in the dialect its program documents
features.acceptance: Through a stub HTTP handler and no socket, an address whose host is not 127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost is refused at construction with its plain reason and nothing is sent; Ollama is asked on /api/chat with model, the two messages, stream false, think false and options.temperature, and format equal to the schema only for a proposal; llama-server is found by /v1/models and asked on /v1/chat/completions with response_format only for a proposal; a model Ollama reports as remote or does not have is refused before anything is sent; no reply within the timeout is refused as no reply and a cancelled question throws OperationCanceledException with no reply surfaced; settings version 3 round-trips where the model runs and a version-2 file gives the defaults and a notice.

features.title: The MLX runtime runs the model in napkin through the bridge's C ABI, and says why when it cannot
features.acceptance: Through a fake bridge and no native library, the MLX runtime checks the bridge's interface version, initialises it with the metallib beside it and loads the folder once, off the calling thread, on the first question; asks with the system prompt alone, the Context/Question user message, thinking off, the schema passed through verbatim and 1024 or 2048 tokens; answers text or a JSON document, refuses in the bridge's own words for an error and in napkin's for running out of room, no Metal device or a question already out; starts the 30-second limit after the load and refuses no reply in time as no reply, while a cancelled question throws OperationCanceledException; unloads exactly once; refuses a model folder missing a file the bridge needs, by name and in the bridge's words; reports MLX unavailable off Apple silicon or without all three of the bridge's files; and the structs are 136 and 40 bytes with the header's offsets, statuses and array sizes.

features.title: A model is downloaded only with consent, from its pinned commit, and every file is checked against its SHA-256
features.acceptance: Through a stub HTTP handler and no socket, the catalog's three models match the Hugging Face Hub as read (repository, 40-hex commit, card licence and every file's name, size and SHA-256, only the loader's *.safetensors/*.json/*.jinja, no .py); a download not told of consent throws before any request; every file is asked for at its https://huggingface.co/<repo>/resolve/<commit>/<file> URL and redirects are followed by napkin, relative ones against their own URL, only over HTTPS to the Hub's documented hosts and at most five times, any other refused naming where; a resume sends Range from the part's length on every hop and appends only a 206 starting there, a 200 starts the file again; more bytes than the catalog's are never written, a short file is kept to resume, a file whose SHA-256 differs is deleted and refused naming it and both hashes; cancel leaves what arrived; the folder is assembled as <folder>.downloading, which is never a model folder, and renamed only when every file passed; something already at the destination is never touched.

features.title: Explain a No data header, then a made-up size is refused
features.acceptance: Opening samples/window-in-existing-wall, selecting Window 1 and asking Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+A why its header is No data shows the good answer whole with the From-napkin block, the disclaimer and the whereabouts line, and a second question whose scripted reply claims a header size napkin never gave it is shown with that sentence replaced by the refusal naming the tokens, the rest of the answer standing; Escape closes the note.

features.title: A help question, thinking watched and cancelled, then asked again
features.acceptance: Asking a free-text question shows the thinking line while a delayed scripted reply is out; Escape cancels it, leaving the note open and empty with no answer; asking again (a cancelled question has used its reply) gets the second scripted reply and shows an answer citing the help item its own reference pack says it should.

features.title: A shopping-list question is answered from the open list's rows
features.acceptance: Opening the stocked-bench sample (whose parts carry stock, unlike coffee-table) and its shopping list with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+L, then asking Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+A how many 2x4s to buy answers with the shopping list's own row numbers, read from the sample's expected fixture, with the row rendered under the answer; a second scripted answer with a made-up count is refused.

features.title: Sketch a bench from words, leave a leg out, then firm it up
features.acceptance: On a new sheet, Assistant → Sketch from words… opens the note for a sketch; describing the quick bench and pressing Enter lists the design note's four rough planks on a sheet with a tick each and draws nothing; unticking Leg 2 with the pointer and pressing Enter draws exactly three rough planks at sketch-mode §7.2's anchors and sizes, 3/4 inch deep, with no stock and no relationship, as one undo step named "Assistant sketch", the note's closing line pointing at Firm up; Ctrl/Cmd+Z empties the sheet and Ctrl/Cmd+Y restores it; F opens Firm up with the two contacts among the three parts and a stock line and a size line for each.

features.title: Edit in words: make a leg 18 inches tall, undo it, then a name matching two parts is refused
features.acceptance: On samples/coffee-table with the south-west leg selected, asking Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+A "make it 18 inches tall" puts the question as an edit (the edit prompt and schema) and lists the scripted reply's two lines on the proposal sheet, ticked, with nothing changed; unticking the rename with the pointer and pressing Enter makes the leg exactly 18 inches long with a ParamValue on its depth driving it, the name kept, as one undo step named "Assistant edit"; Ctrl/Cmd+Z restores 16 1/4 inches with nothing stating the depth and Ctrl/Cmd+Y makes it 18 again; with both long aprons selected by Shift-click, "call these Apron" lists two rename lines and Enter renames both as one more undo step; "call it Apron 9" with the two still selected shows one refused line naming both by their item numbers, its tick off and disabled, and Enter changes nothing and adds no undo step; Escape closes the note.

features.title: Choose a model on this machine, test it and ask it
features.acceptance: With a stub Ollama under the window, Assistant → Where the model runs… refuses another machine's address with nothing sent, lists the stub's models with the size, quantization and license it reports and the cloud model marked as not on this machine, fills the model from the list, Test reports the round trip of an "ok", Use these settings writes settings version 3 and the window's model becomes the local one, and a question asked with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+A is answered on the note with the local whereabouts line after a request to /api/chat with stream and think off and no format.

features.title: Choose MLX on this Mac, test it and ask it
features.acceptance: With a fake bridge under the window and an availability seam forcing MLX available, Assistant → Where the model runs… enables the third radio, choosing it and typing a model folder shows the folder's own words, Test shows a loading line naming the weight size while the fake bridge "loads" and then reports the round trip of an "ok", Use these settings writes settings version 4 with the Mlx provider and the folder and the window's model becomes the MLX one, and a question asked with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+A is answered on the note with the in-napkin whereabouts line naming the folder.

features.title: Download a model only after consent, each file checked against its SHA-256
features.acceptance: With a stub Hub under the window serving small files whose hashes the workflow computed (the real default's repository, commit, licence and file names), choosing MLX shows Download… naming the model, its size and licence; Download… lays a consent sheet over the dialog listing the repository and pinned commit, every file with its size, SHA-256 and pinned URL, the licence and card link and the destination, with nothing sent; Download is disabled and does nothing until the box is ticked; a file served with one wrong byte is refused naming it and both hashes with no folder made; after the server is put right, ticking again and Download fetches only the files that had not passed, the progress reaches the last file, 'Downloaded and checked: 8 files.' shows, the folder box is filled with the new folder and described with the catalog's licence; every request was a pinned URL or the content server it redirected to; Escape closes the sheet and Download… reads Downloaded; Use these settings saves the folder.
